definitions.age_group: Age of main household provider, not the age of each consumer. The provider is the household member aged 16+ with the largest regular contribution to household budget.
definitions.young_people_at_parental_home: A young adult living with an older main provider is classified in that older provider's group. These data cannot describe all young individuals' consumption.
definitions.units: Annual euros, current prices unless explicitly CPI-adjusted
definitions.per_equivalent_unit: OECD-modified scale, adjusts for household size and composition. Main provider=1, additional adult=0.5, child=0.3 according to Idescat notes. It is not the euro amount actually spent by each individual.
definitions.consumption_scope: EPF consumption includes monetary purchases, in-kind spending, own-production and imputed housing rents for owner-occupied/free housing. It excludes home purchase and does not include public health/education transfers in kind. It is not net wealth or cash disposable income.
definitions.comparison: Repeated cross-sections, not the same households or birth cohorts followed over time. Changes can reflect household composition, emancipation, provider mix and sampling.
definitions.wealth_distinction: GDP, income and consumption are flows. None is a stock measure of net household wealth (assets minus liabilities).

comparability.2006_2015: EPF base2006; years2006–2012 revised to Census2011 populations
comparability.2016_break: Official methodology explicitly says2016 results are not directly comparable with preceding years because classification and data-collection changes. Some 2-digit expenditure categories preserve comparability, but no provider-age bridge was established in this research.
comparability.2023_break: Official annual age-table SSV note: Census2021 population update creates a series break that prevents homogeneous comparisons.2023 values marked b.
comparability.2024_break: Official table also flags2024 b; COICOP2018 introduced.2016–20 and2023 classification revised in June2026;2021/22 revisions forthcoming and currently unavailable in revised table.
comparability.safe_chart_option: Use2024 age cross-section as the latest snapshot. If a historic change is desired, use2016→2019 within one base and before COVID, labelled as a historical episode, or2007→2015 within old base. Do not draw a clean2007→2024 growth story or join across breaks.
comparability.cpi_limitation: General Catalan CPI is an approximate common deflator, not an age-specific price index and not the national-accounts consumption deflator. Its basket excludes imputed rent whereas EPF includes it; interpret EPF/CPI as an indicative real-spending proxy, not an exact volume measure. Prefer official national-accounts volume series for aggregate consumption/GDP charts.

real_calculation.precision_note: Published annual CPI index in this official table has1decimal. Derived growth percentages should be called approximate and rounded no more than1decimal.
